summary: Steel lookout on Chemical Road in Parry Sound District; 1963 map shows a 24 m tower; not one of four towers staffed in 1969.

facts.agency: Ontario Department of Lands and Forests
facts.status_note: Sources do not describe what remains at the site.

events.note: Shown as an 80 foot steel tower on the Department of Lands and Forests Tower Detection System Map (1963)
Not among the four towers still actively staffed in 1969 (Ardbeg, Go Home, Stormy Lake, Boulter)

evidence.supports: Parry Sound Forest Fire District founded in 1922 by the Department of Lands and Forests
evidence.quote: The Parry Sound Forest Fire District was founded by Ontario's former Department of Lands and Forests (now the MNR) in 1922

evidence.supports: Purpose of the district: early detection of forest fires from fire towers
evidence.quote: to help protect Ontario's forests from fire by early detection from fire towers

evidence.supports: District headquarters in the town of Parry Sound
evidence.quote: The headquarters for the district were housed in the town of Parry Sound.
It was the central location for 21 fire tower lookouts

evidence.supports: Laurier is listed among the district's lookouts
evidence.quote: Boulter, Lount, Laurier, Strong, Proudfoot, Stisted and Draper.

evidence.supports: Parry Sound fire tower is one of the district's 21 lookouts; it was built on the same site as the modern lookout at 17 George Street
evidence.quote: including the Parry Sound fire tower, which was erected in the same location as the modern lookout tower at 17 George Street

evidence.supports: In 1969 only four towers remained actively staffed; Laurier is not among them
evidence.quote: In 1969 there remained only 4 actively staffed towers: Ardbeg, Go Home, Stormy Lake, and Boulter.

evidence.supports: The article says the four staffed towers were phased out shortly after aerial firefighting came in during the 1970s
evidence.quote: These would all be phased out shortly after when aerial firefighting techniques were employed in the 1970s.

evidence.supports: Location on Chemical Road in unorganized North East Parry Sound, Parry Sound District
evidence.quote: Chemical Road, Unorganized North East Parry Sound, Parry Sound District, Central Ontario, Ontario, Canada

evidence.supports: 1963 Department of Lands and Forests map shows an 80 foot steel tower at the site
evidence.quote: the Department of Lands and Forests Tower Detection System Map (1963) shows an 80 foot steel tower at this location.

evidence.supports: Tower does not appear on the Huntsville topographic map 31E
evidence.quote: Tower does not appear on Huntsville topographic map 31E

notes_for_editor: Two sources. The Wikipedia district article is the only source for the 1922 founding, the list that includes Laurier, and the 1969 staffing count, and it gives no build year for Laurier. The Parry Sound fire tower is one of the 21 district lookouts and stood on the same site as the modern lookout at 17 George Street; keep it separate from Laurier. A search snippet for a Cottage Life article gives 27 towers for the district; that article was not read and is not used. Tower status after the 1963 map is undocumented.
